why: The new Order Principle (prefer the later cut among candidates before the same sentence-final inflection) changed which positions are ranked top‑1 versus top‑2/3: rank_depth fell at depth‑1 (−0.419) while improving depths 2–4, so the edit shuffled the very top choice and harmed short budgets and overall H_set (by_bin shows larger drops for longer bins). Concretely, it caused cuts to be placed inside phrases or before punctuation in some sentences (splitting pronouns/particles or detaching punctuation), producing the large negative tail movements.
lesson: Constrain the Order Principle so it never chooses cuts that split tokens/close dependents or move the single top choice for short-latency budgets; verify effects separately on top‑1 and long‑budget bins.
